key_insight: Ceramics are governed by a processing–microstructure–property chain in which atomic bonding, defects, porosity, and phase stability jointly determine mechanical, thermal, electrical, and biomedical performance.
engineering_relevance: The review shows how controlling sintering, sol–gel routes, and additive manufacturing can tailor densification, geometry, and composition to improve ceramic performance in structural and biomedical applications.
method: Review of crystal chemistry, defects, grain size, porosity, and residual stresses
Comparison of conventional sintering, sol–gel processing, and additive manufacturing
Coverage of biomedical ceramics, nanoceramics, composites, and smart/functional materials
evidence_signal: The paper synthesizes literature rather than presenting new experimental data, organizing evidence around the processing–microstructure–property–performance framework.
watch_item: Ceramics remain limited by brittle fracture and the porosity–strength trade-off, so processing improvements must avoid introducing heterogeneity or unstable degradation behavior.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
